title: Maryam, whole
hookLine: Zakariyya, Maryam, Ibrahim, Musa, Isma'il, Idris (Surah 19)
tomorrow: why would God tell Musa to take off his shoes?

lines: A SURAH NAMED FOR A WOMAN.
cards: Every group project has the question that starts the argument: who counts as a lead?
The Qur'an has a surah named for a woman, Maryam, the mother of Isa, and it carries a question classical scholars argued over in plain sight. Was she a prophet?
The surah opens, in Pickthall's words: "A mention of the mercy of thy Lord unto His servant Zachariah." And then it keeps going, person after person, mercy after mercy, until the end.

teach.b: Read it whole and the shape is a procession. Zakariyya, old, crying to his Lord in secret for a child, and given Yahya.

Maryam, alone, visited by the angel, giving birth beneath a palm, and the baby who speaks from the cradle. Then Ibrahim pleading gently with his father, Musa called near, Isma'il true to his promise, Idris raised high.
Through all of it a name keeps coming back: ar-Rahman, the Beneficent. Now the debate. Maryam's section opens the way the prophets' sections do: "And make mention of Mary in the Scripture."
One view, held by some classical scholars, Ibn Hazm among them: yes, she was a prophet. An angel spoke to her, and God's word came to her; what else is prophecy?

teach.h: THE SAME OPENING AS THE PROPHETS.
teach.b: The other view: prophethood was given to men, and the surah calls Ibrahim, Musa, Isma'il and Idris prophets in so many words, but not her.

teach.h: YES: AN ANGEL SPOKE TO HER.
teach.b: Another verse calls her siddiqa, a woman of truth.
Both views honor her; the Qur'an says she was chosen above the women of the worlds. Neither side lowers her by an inch; the argument is over a title, not over her place.
What the surah itself insists on is the thread: mercy, passed from one person to the next. A child given to an old man. A mother fed by a palm tree.
Whatever the title, the mercy moves through each of them.

how: Surah Maryam is recited in Arabic in prayer and at home; Muslims honor Maryam as the mother of Isa, and scholars have held different views on whether she should be called a prophet.

s: a whole surah of the Qur'an is named for Maryam
surah 19, which opens with mercy and walks through the prophets.
the surah calls Maryam a prophet in so many words
her section opens like the prophets' sections, but it names the men prophets outright. scholars weighed that differently.
the Qur'an's Maryam is a different woman from the Gospels' Mary
she is Maryam, mother of Isa: the Mary whom Christians also honor.

games.q: your friend holds that Maryam was a prophet. she asks you for the best case for the other view. what do you give her?
o: she was a woman, and the Qur'an rarely talks about women at all.
she never heard from an angel, so nothing was revealed to her.
the surah names the men prophets outright, and another verse calls her a woman of truth.
games.why: that's the strongest form of the 'no' view: the surah's explicit titles, and siddiqa in 5:75. the 'yes' view answers that an angel spoke to her. both honor her.

practice: Read the surah's first line aloud, slowly: a mention of the mercy of thy Lord unto His servant Zachariah.
Then, for the sit, bring to mind one person whose kindness reached you without any title attached, and let them stand in the procession for a while.

wordCard.voice: Maryam. The mother of Isa, and the name of a whole surah that walks through the prophets on a road paved with mercy.

carryVoice: The line to keep: mercy through the prophets, whatever title each one carries. Surah Maryam, read aloud.
